page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highmem-4 is an instance configuration within the compute-optimized C2D family, provisioned with an elevated memory-to-core allocation. Powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7B13 processor, the server supplies 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core. Hardware specifications include 32.0 GB of system memory, equating to 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage is not bundled locally, necessitating network-attached persistent storage for persistent file systems, and the configuration includes no dedicated GPUs and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. CPU cache resources consist of 32 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache, with hardware support for AES, VAES, SHA-NI, and AVX instructions.

Benchmark analysis demonstrates a clear bifurcation between single-threaded efficiency and parallel capacity. In single-core testing, the c2d-highmem-4 records strong stress-ng computation in the top 25% tier, supported by middle-tier Geekbench single-core and PassMark CPU overall scores. However, aggregate multi-threaded benchmarks—including Geekbench multi-core, software compilation using Clang, and PassMark database operations—place into the lower 25% bracket, directly constrained by the two-physical-core ceiling. Memory benchmarks demonstrate mid-range uncached throughput at 46.82 GB/sec for reads and 27.55 GB/sec for writes, while small cached reads align lower relative to high-core platforms.

From an infrastructure perspective, this instance profile presents favorable cost efficiency when hosting memory-demanding applications that do not require wide multi-core parallelism. The high 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio avoids the necessity of over-provisioning compute resources merely to satisfy large operational memory footprints. Tradeoffs include the lack of local NVMe storage and absence of advanced matrix instructions like AVX-512. The server functions efficiently for caching systems such as Redis, lightweight relational databases, in-memory analytics jobs, and memory-heavy web application servers.

Equipped with an elevated 32.0 GB of system memory, the instance delivers 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, while offering no bundled local storage, zero dedicated GPUs, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Benchmark testing highlights strong single-core compute performance in the top quartile of stress-ng results, accompanied by average memory bandwidth and overall single-threaded execution. In contrast, multi-core throughput across Geekbench, software compilation, and database operations ranks lower due to the modest physical core budget. The instance provides resource efficiency for memory-dependent processes that do not justify high core counts, making it a reliable fit for memory-intensive backend services, in-memory caching tiers, and lightweight database systems.
